units.zh: 古者太史掌敘邦國之世次，辨其姓氏，別其昭穆，尚失。
units.en: Even in ancient times the Grand Historian who ordered the ages of the realms, sorted clan names, and marked senior from junior lines could not keep the record whole.
units.literal: In antiquity the Grand Historian kept the generations of the states, distinguished their surnames, and separated zhao from mu—and still there were lapses.

units.zh: 金人初起完毅十二部，其後皆以部為氏，史臣記錄有稱「宗室」者，有稱完顏者。
units.en: The Jin first gathered in the twelve Wanyi tribes, then took each tribe as a clan name. Court historians sometimes wrote "Imperial Clan", sometimes Wanyan.
units.literal: When the Jin people first arose in the twelve tribes of Wanyi, afterward all took their tribe as surname; in the historians' records some are called "Imperial Clan", some Wanyan.

units.zh: 稱完顏者亦有二焉，有同姓完顏，蓋疏族，若石土門、迪古乃是也；
units.en: "Wanyan" itself split two ways: same-surname Wanyan were really distant kin, men like Shitumen and Digunai;
units.literal: Those called Wanyan also fall into two kinds: same-surname Wanyan, who were in fact collateral kin—Shitumen and Digunai are examples;

units.zh: 有異姓完顏，蓋部人，若歡都是也。
units.en: different-surname Wanyan were really tribesmen, men like Huandu.
units.literal: and different-surname Wanyan, who were in fact men of the tribe—Huandu is an example.

units.zh: 大定以前稱「宗室」，明昌以後避睿宗諱稱「內族」，其實一而已，書名不書氏，其制如此。
units.en: Before Dading they were called "Imperial Clan"; after Mingchang, to avoid the taboo on Ruizong, "Inner Kin"—the same group in fact. Registers record personal names, not clan names; that was the rule.
units.literal: Before the Dading era they were called "Imperial Clan"; after Mingchang, to avoid the taboo on Ruizong they were called "Inner Kin"—in substance one and the same. The annals give personal names, not clan names; such was the rule.

units.zh: 宣宗詔宗室皆稱完顏，不復識別焉。
units.en: Emperor Xuanzong ordered that all imperial kin take the name Wanyan, and the old distinctions ceased.
units.literal: Emperor Xuanzong decreed that all of the imperial clan should be called Wanyan, and no further distinction was made.

units.zh: 大定、泰和之間，袒免以上親皆有屬籍，以敘授官，大功以上，薨卒輟朝，親親之道行焉。
units.en: From Dading through Taihe, relatives within tan-mian degree and nearer were entered in the clan rolls and ranked for appointment; when one within da-gong degree or nearer died, court paused in mourning—kinship was honored in deed.
units.literal: Between Dading and Taihe, kin within the degree of tan-mian mourning and closer all had household registers, by which offices were assigned; for kin within the degree of da-gong mourning and closer, death halted court audiences—the way of cherishing kin was practiced.

units.zh: 貞祐以後，譜牒散失，大概僅存，不可殫悉，今掇其可次第者著於篇。
units.en: After Zhenyou the pedigree books were lost; a broken outline alone remains, too fragmentary to exhaust. Here I collect what can still be sequenced and place it in these pages.
units.literal: After Zhenyou the genealogical registers were scattered and lost; only a rough outline survives, and it cannot be set forth in full. Now I gather what can be ordered by generation and set it down in this chapter.

units.zh: 其上無所系、下無所承者，不能盡錄也。
units.en: Lines that attach to nothing above and hand down to nothing below cannot be entered in full.
units.literal: Those with no tie above and no succession below cannot all be recorded.

units.en: Fang (Deputy Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs).
units.literal: Fang (Deputy Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs).

units.zh: 胡八魯（穆宗孫，寧州刺史。）
units.en: Hubalu (grandson of Muzong; Prefect of Ningzhou).
units.literal: Hubalu (grandson of Muzong; Prefect of Ningzhou).

units.en: Qi (Military Commissioner of the Lishe Army).
units.literal: Qi (Military Commissioner of the Lishe Army).

units.zh: 拔離速（宗室子。元帥左監軍。）
units.en: Balisu (imperial clansman; Marshal Left Supervisor of the Army).
units.literal: Balisu (imperial clansman; Marshal Left Supervisor of the Army).

units.zh: 銀术可（拔離族子。同中書門下平章事。）
units.en: Yinshuake (kinsman of the Balisu clan; Fellow Associate Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery).
units.literal: Yinshuake (kinsman of the Balisu clan; Fellow Associate Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery).

units.zh: 麻吉（銀术可弟。銀青光祿大夫。）
units.en: Maji (younger brother of Yinshuake; Silver Radiance Grand Master of Splendid Happiness).
units.literal: Maji (younger brother of Yinshuake; Silver Radiance Grand Master of Splendid Happiness).

units.zh: 宗賢（本名阿魯。太祖從姪。婆速路兵馬都緫管。）
units.en: Zongxian (born Alu; Taizu's nephew by the collateral line; Commander of the Bosu-route military).
units.literal: Zongxian (born Alu; Taizu's nephew by the collateral line; Commander of the Bosu-route military).

units.zh: 右諸宗室可譜者凡十一族，雖稱系出某帝，而不能世次，不譜於各帝之下，所以慎也。
units.en: Listed at right: of the imperial kin who can be entered in a pedigree, eleven clans in all; though they are said to stem from a given emperor, their generations cannot be fixed, so they are not entered under each emperor's line — hence the caution.
units.literal: At right: of the imperial kin who can be entered in a pedigree, eleven clans in all; though they are said to stem from a given emperor, their generations cannot be fixed, so they are not entered under each emperor's line — hence the caution.

units.zh: 列傳第六 ○歡都子 謀演 冶訶子 阿魯補 骨赧 訛古乃 蒲查
units.en: Biographies 6: Huandu and his son Mouyan; Yehe and his sons Alubu, Gunan, and Egunai; Sanda's son Pucha
units.literal: Biographies 6: Huandu and his son Mouyan; Yehe and his sons Alubu, Gunan, and Egunai; Sanda's son Pucha

units.zh: 冶訶子阿魯補、骨赧、訛古乃、散荅。
units.en: Yehe's sons were Alubu, Gunan, Egunai, and Sanda.
units.literal: Yehe's sons were Alubu, Gunan, Egunai, and Sanda.

units.zh: 至景祖時，石魯之子劾孫舉部來歸，居於安出虎水源胡凱山南。
units.en: In Jingzu's day Shilu's son Hesun brought his tribe in submission and settled south of Hukai Mountain on the headwaters of the Anchu River.
units.literal: In the time of Jingzu, Shilu's son Hesun brought his whole tribe to submit and dwelt south of Hukai Mountain on the Anchu River.

units.zh: 睿宗立德顯仁啟聖廣運文武簡肅皇帝諱宗堯，初諱宗輔，本諱訛裏朵，大定上尊諡，追上今諱。
units.en: Ruizong—posthumously the Virtuous, Manifest, Initiating-Sagacity, Broad-Fortune, Literary-Martial, Simple-and-Solemn Emperor—was taboo-named Zongyao, first Zongfu, born Woliduo; in the Dading era his honors were raised and he received the name he bears now.
units.literal: Ruizong, posthumous title Virtuous Manifest Benevolence Initiating Sagacity Broad Fortune Literary Martial Simple Solemn Emperor, taboo name Zongyao, at first taboo name Zongfu, original taboo name Woliduo; under Dading posthumous honors were raised and his present taboo name was granted.

units.zh: 世宗即位，追上尊諡立德顯仁啟聖廣運文武簡肅皇帝，廟號睿宗。
units.en: At Shizong's accession he received the full posthumous title and the temple name Ruizong.
units.literal: When Shizong took the throne, posthumous honors were raised to the Virtuous Manifest Benevolence Initiating Sagacity Broad Fortune Literary Martial Simple Solemn Emperor, with temple name Ruizong.

units.zh: 以八月往陝西，或使宗弼遂將以行，或宗輔、宗幹、希尹中以一人往。」
units.en: In the eighth month march on Shaanxi—either Zongbi leads the whole way, or one of Zongfu, Zonggan, and Xiyin goes."
units.literal: In the eighth month go to Shaanxi—either have Zongbi lead the army through, or send one among Zongfu, Zonggan, and Xiyin."

units.zh: 十三年，行次媯州薨，年四十，陪葬睿陵，追封潞王，諡襄穆。
units.en: In Tianhui 13, he died while traveling through Guizhou at the age of forty. He was buried beside Ruiling and posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Lu, with the posthumous name Xiangmu.
units.literal: In Tianhui 13, he died while traveling through Guizhou, aged forty; he was buried beside Ruiling and posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Lu, with the posthumous name Xiangmu.

units.en: In the sixth year of Huangtong he was raised to Prince of Ji.
units.literal: In the sixth year of Huangtong he was advanced to Prince of Ji.

units.zh: 正隆二年，追贈太師、上柱國，改封許王。
units.en: In the second year of Zhenlong he was posthumously made grand preceptor and upper pillar of state and enfeoffed as Prince of Xu.
units.literal: In the second year of Zhenlong he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor and Upper Pillar of State and enfeoffed as Prince of Xu.

units.zh: 天會五年，宗望薨，帝為右副元帥，駐兵燕京。
units.en: In the fifth year of Tianhui Zongwang died; the emperor became right deputy commander-in-chief and stationed troops at Yanjing.
units.literal: In the fifth year of Tianhui Zongwang died; the emperor became right deputy commander-in-chief and stationed troops at Yanjing.

units.zh: 十一月，分遣諸將伐宋，帝發自河間，徇地淄、青。
units.en: In the eleventh month the generals were divided and sent against Song; the emperor set out from Hejian and pacified Zi and Qing.
units.literal: In the eleventh month the generals were divided and sent against Song; the emperor set out from Hejian and pacified Zi and Qing.

units.zh: 帝至富平，婁室為左翼，宗弼為右翼，兩軍並進，自日中至於昏暮，凡六合戰，破之。
units.en: At Fuping Lou Shi took the left and Zongbi the right; both wings pressed from noon to dusk, fought six rounds, and shattered Zhang Jun.
units.literal: The emperor reached Fuping; Lou Shi held the left wing and Zongbi the right; both armies advanced together from midday until dusk, fought six engagements, and broke the enemy.

units.zh: 太祖征伐四方，諸子皆總戎旅，帝常在帷幄。
units.en: While Taizu warred in every direction his sons led armies; the emperor himself usually kept to the command tent.
units.literal: When Taizu campaigned on every side, his sons all commanded armies, but the emperor often stayed within the command tent.

units.zh: 天輔六年，太祖親征，太宗居黃龍府，安福哥誘新降之民以叛，帝與烏古乃討平之。
units.en: In the sixth year of Tianfu, while Taizu marched in person and Taizong held Huanglong Prefecture, Anfuge stirred newly submitted folk to revolt; the emperor and Wugunai crushed them.
units.literal: In the sixth year of Tianfu, when Taizu campaigned in person and Taizong held Huanglong Prefecture, Anfuge incited newly submitted people to rebel; the emperor and Wugunai put the rising down.

units.zh: 六年正月，宋馬括兵二十萬至樂安，帝率師擊破之。
units.en: In the first month of the sixth year Song general Ma Kuo with two hundred thousand troops reached Le'an; the emperor led his army and defeated them.
units.literal: In the first month of the sixth year Song general Ma Kuo with two hundred thousand troops reached Le'an; the emperor led his army and defeated them.

units.zh: 帝發自河北，降滑州，取開德府，攻大名府，克之，河北平。
units.en: The emperor set out from Hebei, reduced Huazhou, took Kaide Prefecture, attacked Daming Prefecture, captured it, and Hebei was pacified.
units.literal: The emperor set out from Hebei, reduced Huazhou, took Kaide Prefecture, attacked Daming Prefecture, captured it, and Hebei was pacified.

units.zh: 於是班師，與宗翰俱朝京師，立熙宗為諳版勃極烈，帝為左副元帥。
units.en: They withdrew to court; with Zonghan they installed Hela as an-ban boji lie and made the emperor left deputy commander-in-chief.
units.literal: The army then withdrew; together with Zonghan he came to court, Hela was installed as an-ban boji lie, and the emperor became left deputy commander-in-chief.

units.zh: 二年，改葬於大房山，號景陵。
units.en: In the second year his tomb was moved to Great Fang Mountain, called Jingling.
units.literal: In the second year he was reburied on Great Fang Mountain, tomb name Jingling.

units.en: Massive and imposing, he made men afraid at a glance.
units.literal: Towering and august, men looked on him and feared.

units.en: He was forgiving by nature, generous in giving, and held honesty dear.
units.literal: By nature forgiving, fond of bestowing favors, and devoted to honesty.

units.zh: 宗翰伐宋，圍太原未下，宗翰還西京，骨赧以右翼軍佐銀術可守太原。
units.en: When Zonghan marched on Song he besieged Taiyuan without success and returned to the Western Capital. Gunan held Taiyuan with the right wing under Yinshu Ke.
units.literal: Zonghan campaigned against Song and besieged Taiyuan without taking it; Zonghan returned to the Western Capital; Gunan with the right wing assisted Yinshu Ke in defending Taiyuan.

units.zh: 子喜哥襲猛安，加宣武將軍。
units.en: His son Xige inherited the meng'an and was made General of Manifest Martiality.
units.literal: His son Xige inherited the meng'an and was made General of Manifest Martiality.
